mission_05: Seasonal decomposition is a fundamental technique for understanding the underlying structure of time series data by separating it into distinct components: trend, seasonality, and residuals. The trend component captures the long-term progression of the series, the seasonal component represents regular periodic fluctuations that repeat at fixed intervals, and the residual component contains the irregular noise that cannot be explained by trend or seasonality. Two decomposition models are commonly used: the additive model where Y = Trend + Seasonal + Residual, appropriate when seasonal variations are constant over time, and the multiplicative model where Y = Trend * Seasonal * Residual, suitable when seasonal variations grow or shrink proportionally with the level of the series. In this mission, you will implement both decomposition methods using moving averages for trend estimation, compute seasonal indices by averaging detrended values at each seasonal position, and reconstruct the original series from its components.
